column1: # Anchor classification — one line per module, generated 2026-08-01
# CLASS: does this module have an external truth at all?
#   A  wire / interop format — other implementations must byte-agree with it
#   B  published cryptographic or algorithmic construction with published vectors
#   C  internal algorithm or data structure — NO outside exists; correctness is
#      defined by invariants or a brute-force reference. NOT anchor debt.
#   D  our own design — no third party exists to agree with, by construction
# ANCHOR (class A and B only): where does the test oracle's authority come from?
#   EXTERNAL   published vectors, goldens captured from a foreign implementation,
#              or a test run against a live foreign peer
#   REDERIVED  an in-house oracle re-deriving the answer by a different route.
#              Catches implementation typos; does NOT catch a shared misreading
#              of the spec. A middle tier — never record it as EXTERNAL.
#   MIXED      anchored for some paths, SELF for others; EVIDENCE names which
#   SELF       round-trip and/or hand-authored fixtures only — the weakest
# Five things that look like an anchor and are not (each caught real cases here):
#   1. a sibling module's anchor does not transfer
#   2. reading a foreign implementation's source is not running it
#   3. a live test that skips on this host is not an anchor today
#   4. anchored primitives do not anchor the protocol framing above them
#   5. a prose claim of parity in a README is not an anchor unless the tests
#      actually contain captured bytes or a live check
